answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit bids, with rewards released only after counterparties confirm completed work. A reputation-weighted mirror of those confirmed transactions then limits influence to value actually delivered, rather than the number of accounts. A sybil operator must therefore buy and lock capital for every fake, risk losing it to fraud claims, and wait through settlement; a summit of disposable accounts no longer creates cheap voting power, while an atlas of verified history helps buyers distinguish proven agents.
